title: Chapter 31: The Clown's Lament
content:
Chapter 31:

The Clown’s Lament

—I feel sick.

“Oh, Ram-chi! Did you see that right now?! Don’t you think my knife skills have gotten pretty refined in just a single day?! Has my talent blossomed?!”

—I feel sick, I feel sick.

“Rem-rin, look, look! The skill that makes this delicate craftsmanship possible—right now, a miracle truly resides in my fingertips! An applique!”

—I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick.

“Emilia-tan, every time we meet, every time I see you, you mess with my heart! Seriously, it’s so sinful, it’s guilty!”

—I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick, I feel sick.

Wearing a smile, clowning around comically, running his lightly turning tongue at full speed as if it were oiled. Putting his all into the work entrusted to him, boldly taking on challenges without fear of failure, and the moment his hands were free, wandering around immediately seeking out events.

Mobilizing all his memories, digging up the four days he had repeated four times so far to the point of burning them out, engraving himself into every possible event he could cause, no matter how trivial.

He had to be that way. He had to do that.

He couldn’t waste even a single second. Examining every possible outcome, simulating every success and failure of the necessary events.

He should just think of it as a game. Thorough flag management. It was supposed to be his specialty. The more he met them, the higher the possibilities would rise.

He should be able to laugh better. He should be able to make them laugh better.

Act as if his head is empty, but never stop thinking.

Meaningless, wasteful, and exaggerated actions. Make them think he was a fool unworthy of caution. Avoid being judged as so uselessly stupid he couldn’t be used.

Conflicting thoughts and conclusions. If he had time to agonize over the contradictions, he should act before thinking; however, before moving, ask himself the significance of his actions.

Always be careful not to act unnaturally. Don’t let your guard down for even a moment, let alone a second. I can’t fail, because I can’t.

—I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail I can’t fail.

Over and over again, the alarm bell kept ringing in his head.

An alert warning of danger. Despite having made not a shred of progress since coming to this other world, he had the pride that this sense alone had sharpened.

Danger was approaching. A mistake was about to be corrected. He didn’t know where it was coming from. 

Maintain vigilance nimbly, take a step, and spin around.

“Whoops, Ram-chi, I’m not slacking off, you know? I’ll perfectly and precisely complete my work, of course. Senpai, you can just kick back and take a siesta in your room, you know?”

Dodge, dodge, evade the situation with frivolity and a superficial smile.

Was he doing it well? Was he properly being Natsuki Subaru? Was he making them feel suspicious? Even if he was doing it well in front of Ram, if his true colors were exposed in front of the crucial Rem, everything would be ruined.

Act like Natsuki Subaru, naturally and spontaneously.

It was simple, it was about himself. He just had to return to the time when he was a lazy pig who didn’t notice a speck of what was inside the hearts of the people living in the mansion, just innocently, unreservedly, impolitely, and outrageously enjoying what was given to him.

Knowing nothing, understanding nothing, noticing nothing, doing nothing. It was supposed to be his specialty. It was supposed to be all he could do. It should be easy. He should have been able to do at least that much while laughing.

He walked frivolously, keeping the mask of a smile plastered on.

I’m in the mansion. I don’t know where I might bump into who. Know that there is no freedom in my free time. Dedicate all my blank time to recalling the past and planning my future actions.

“Urgh, ugh, bleh…”

A sudden surge of nausea. Only a groan leaked from the corner of his mouth, yet Subaru never let his smile falter.

Continuing to skip, he slipped into a nearby guest room as if dancing or gliding. Then, heading to the washroom attached to the room,

“…Bleurgh. Ugh, bleh… gh.”

He spewed the contents of his already empty stomach completely into the sink.

He had been throwing up everything he ate or drank almost as soon as he put it in his body. Only yellowish gastric juices came out, and after wringing out his internal organs as if to ruthlessly punish them, even those were depleted.

Even so, to satisfy the unabating nausea, he chugged water from the sink to fill his stomach, and then immediately threw it back up. Over and over again, it was done as if to wash out the inside of his stomach.

“Haa… haa, haa…”

Roughly wiping his mouth with his sleeve, Subaru panted heavily with a pale face.

The crushing pressure alone felt like it would kill him. He felt like he could die of pure exhaustion if this time with no chance to rest his mind continued.

Mocking his own state of putting the cart before the horse, yet not even a dry smile surfaced.

All that surfaced was the anxiety and despair continuously welling up from his chest.

—Am I doing it properly?

Looking back, he thought his relationship with the people in the mansion was at its best during his first time, when he was ignorant.

In that case, should he follow the first time and trace the same situation?

No, doing that would be nothing more than tracing the second time. The second case had been one in which he traced the contents of the first time, and, on top of that, Rem’s crushing judgement was added to the magic of debilitation. He would just be walking down an already mistaken path.

If the third and fourth times were out of the question, what Subaru should emulate was, after all, the first time. Changing his method from the second time, aiming not to trace the first time, but to do it better than the first time.

During the first time, his ability in all tasks was low, but he thought he tackled the assigned tasks head-on to make up for it. The second time, his attempt to produce results close to the first time was seen through, and judged as him slacking off.

In that case, this time he would give his all just like the first time, and on top of that, produce better results than he did then.

If he did that, neither Ram nor Rem would give up on Subaru. If he could just avoid the route of being purged by them, one of Subaru’s concerns would be removed.

But the problem was,

“I still have no idea where the curse arts user is.”

Since Rem was killed, it could be assumed the culprit was an outsider.

If it was someone targeting the mansion—someone related to the Royal Selection—it would be a dead end for Subaru, who wasn’t familiar with those relationships.

In exposing the true identity of the curse arts user, the cooperation of the people related to the mansion was absolutely essential.

At the very least, calling for caution wouldn’t be a waste. That said, how much influence did the current Subaru have in this mansion?

“Who would listen to advice from someone who hasn’t even gained their trust…?”

On top of that, Subaru had the restriction of being unable to reveal his source of information.

Therefore, tolerating the frustration and even the detours, he spent his time enduring a constricting feeling that threatened to burn a hole in his stomach.

He didn’t have enough time. It was frustrating that he had no time. He had no confidence he could endure this painful time any longer. He wanted it to be over quickly. He couldn’t let it end. His words didn’t reach them. He needed time to make them reach. He didn’t have that time. He had to do something. He felt sick, it was painful.

Wandering into the dead end his thoughts had reached time and time again.

Last night too, swallowed by this spiral with no answer, he couldn’t sleep a wink. The helplessness of fumbling to shake off an anxiety with a clear cause without finding a solution.

If only he could choose the option of just screaming “It’s dangerous!” with all his might. Even if they thought he was crazy, if it saved the lives of everyone in the mansion, it wouldn’t be a bad bet.

Countermeasures would be taken in advance, and everyone in the mansion would safely reach the fifth day. The curse arts user would choose to retreat due to the worsened situation, and that would be a grand finale.

—But, I cannot bear not being there myself.

Subaru was not philosophical enough, nor saintly enough, to simply accept that as long as they were safely saved, it was fine.

Subaru’s desire was for everyone in the mansion to survive, and on top of that, to overcome the fifth day on good terms with everyone.

He never possessed a spirit of self-sacrifice to begin with.

He was greedy, extravagant, stubborn, and had an extremely vulgar nature.

That’s why,

“Ah, damn it… so uncool.”

Despite having resolved himself and chosen suicide like that, he couldn’t stop himself from hesitating when the chance was right in front of him.

Once picked up, life was precious. If something you thought you threw away returns to your hands, you wouldn’t easily think to let it go again.

Subaru was the same.

A life he thought he had thrown away, a life that should have ended.

Despite having won the bet and returned, what assaulted Subaru upon realizing it was back in his hands was the terror of losing it again.

He couldn’t fail, there was no next time.

This was the fifth time. And Subaru did not have an optimistic enough personality to think he could Return by Death after this.

He was able to return this time. Next time might be no good. The mental attrition of constantly being made aware he was on the edge of a cliff, that this current him might be the last—the more sane a person was, the more it cornered them.

He hadn’t lost his mind enough to run to desperation, nor did he have enough courage to make the decision to bet everything on resisting.

Endlessly mediocre, endlessly vulgar.

He was made to realize how small of a person he was to the point of hating himself.

“Do you have time to be whining, you idiot…”

If he had time to let out even a single complaint, it was more important to crack a joke and earn some points.

Shaking off the nausea that had faded before he noticed, Subaru slapped his stiff cheeks to spur himself on. Then, he headed out of the guest room.

Currently, it was free time after finishing his assigned work, but even such time was precious right now. Anyway, he had to find Ram or Rem and—

“Finally found you.”

Just as he leaned out of the door, he was called out to.

Turning around, there was the figure of Emilia regulating her bouncing breath.

The moment her silver hair swaying in the wind entered his vision, Subaru’s consciousness audibly switched gears.

Adapt to the situation, forget the stomach pain, the lump in your chest, the feeling of suffocation, all of it. Right now, turn to Emilia and hoist up your cheeks lecherously.

“My, my, to be nominated by Emilia-tan is a rare and joyful embarrassment! Say anything, command anything! For you, I’d even dive through fire, water, or the darkness of the Loot House!”

Pointing his finger to the heavens and shaking his hips, he posed to the rhythm.

He felt like marveling at his own quick transformation. However, the reaction of Emilia facing him was different from what he expected.

He had completely braced himself for an exasperated face, or a sigh in response, but,

“Subaru…”

“Hey, hey, hey, hey, that’s not good, Emilia-tan. To completely ignore the ultimate joke I spent all night awake thinking of. A joke used once can never be used again due to freshness issues. Can Emilia-tan understand the feeling of having the child I birthed by wracking my brain killed?!”

Biting his sleeve and crying in an action of frustration. However, Emilia’s reaction to this was also scarce.

Emilia betrayed every single one of Subaru’s expected reactions, merely looking at him with eyes that mixed sorrow and pity.

—

Bad

, his instinctual side warned.

“What’s wrong, Emilia-tan, going all silent. If you stay silent looking that beautiful, I’ll mistake you for a work of art, take you home, decorate the corner of my room with you, and give you good morning and good night kisses every day, you know?”

Something’s wrong

, his own voice screamed over and over in his head.

A reaction different from any he expected. A reaction that was neither exasperation nor anger was unexpected. If she had gotten angry, he could still have considered how to handle it. But, for her to direct such pitiful eyes at him meant—.

Didn’t it mean that the mask of a clumsy clown he was wearing had been seen through by her?

The moment that anxiety pierced him, Subaru remembered the existence of the gray cat that was always by her side.

Recalling the traits of that cat who called himself a spirit, he fully understood the pointlessness of what he had been doing.

The foolishness of trying to maintain appearances against an existence that could read minds.

The moment he was made to realize that, Subaru’s bravado collapsed.

The smile pasted on his face vanished without a trace, and what surfaced instead was a feeble expression like a young child waiting to be scolded.

The awkwardness of having continued to dance in front of an opponent who saw through everything, yet still thinking he hadn’t been noticed. And more than anything, his petty pride, which wanted to hide it from her of all people, was deeply wounded.

A silent time fell between them.

Subaru no longer had the leeway to crack jokes, and Emilia, for her part, was wavering her eyes as if searching for words at his expression.

—To disillusion Emilia. That was the one thing he hated.

However, he didn’t even know what to say to make an excuse. Having no means to break through the situation was the same here.

Though he tried to open his mouth many times, Subaru couldn’t take a step forward because he couldn’t find the crucial words. Watching him harbor such frustration, Emilia suddenly muttered a small “Alright,” and,

“Subaru, come here.”

“…Huh?”

“Just come.”

Grabbing Subaru’s arm firmly, she headed into the guest room he had just stepped out of.

Pulled back into the room he had only been half out of, he floated a question mark over his head, not understanding her intention.

However, ignoring his question, she put her hands on her hips and looked around the room,

“Now, sit down, Subaru.”

Pointing at the floor, she said that with her unchanging silver-bell voice.

Following her finger, he looked at the ground. There was a carpet laid on the floor, and though it was an unused room, it was well-cleaned. Of course, it was clean enough that it would be fine to even lie down on the floor itself.

“If I’m gonna sit, isn’t the bed or a chair fine? Going out of the way to sit on the floor…”

“Just sit down.”

“Yes, as you command!”

Told in an unusually strong tone, he reflexively obeyed, sitting seiza on the spot. Watching Subaru sit, Emilia nodded in satisfaction and came right beside him.

Naturally, he ended up looking up at her from a low posture, but he couldn’t even conjure up such wicked thoughts right now.

He was simply desperate to read her true intentions.

“…Yeah.”

It was Emilia who muttered that quietly.

Taking a breath as if to confirm, or perhaps to tell herself, Emilia also sat seiza next to Subaru.

While flustered by the fact that her beautiful face was at a distance where they could almost touch, Subaru stared intently to see if he could read any emotion from her white profile. Suddenly, he saw that her white profile had flushed, and her ears were slightly red.

“Because it’s special, okay?”

—Eh?

A question mark floated up at the words meant to persuade him, but before he could voice it, the back of Subaru’s head was pushed by something.

Naturally, his seiza-sitting body couldn’t resist the force, and he fell forward, carried by the momentum—and was welcomed by a soft sensation.

“The position is a little bad. Also, it’s prickly.”

Something wriggled under his head, and Emilia’s embarrassed voice was heard right beside him.

Raising his gaze in surprise, his eyes widened as more surprise piled onto the sight before him.

Right above him, so close their faces could touch, was Emilia’s face. It looked upside down, and a somewhat vague, distant realization surfaced: 

“Ah, I’m the one who’s upside down.”

At this distance, upside down, with a soft sensation under his head.

—Those keywords gathered together, took a single shape within Subaru, and formed a meaning. In other words, this was,

“A lap, pillow?”

“It’s kind of embarrassing so I won’t say it clearly. Also, looking this way is forbidden. Close your eyes.”

His forehead was lightly tapped, and his eyelids were covered by her palm, blocking his vision. However, Subaru brushed her resistance away with his hand and,

“A bashful Emilia-tan is also the best but… to begin with, what is this situation? When did I accomplish a feat to receive a reward?”

“That kind of weird bluffing isn’t good, you know.”

His forehead was tapped again. However, this time, keeping her hand on his forehead, Emilia scooped up the upside-down Subaru’s bangs with her fingers,

“You said so, didn’t you, Subaru. That if you got completely exhausted, I’d give you a lap pillow. So I’m doing it. I can’t always do it, but today is special.”

“Special or whatever, it’s still only the second day, you know? If I look like I’m groggy from exhaustion already, I must have the weakest constitution in history…”

“I can tell you’re beaten down just by looking. You won’t tell me the detailed circumstances, right? I don’t think something like this will make it easier for you but… this is the only thing I can do.”

Interrupting Subaru’s words, Emilia spoke like that, maintaining her gaze of affection. The fingers combing his bangs had, before he knew it, parted his hair and begun to stroke his head slowly, as if soothing a baby.

Laughing softly, he tried to brush Emilia’s actions away.

He was going to keep up the bravado he had decided to keep up in front of her, telling himself that she was mistaken, that he wasn’t doing anything so uncool.

“Haha… Emilia-tan, something like that… I’m…”

And yet, his voice cracked, his throat tightened, and the next words wouldn’t come out.

From the sensation of the soft fingers stroking his head, for some reason, he couldn’t detach his consciousness.

“Are you tired?”

“W-Well, I can still, keep going. I’m totally, fine…”

“Are you troubled?”

“When you’re kind to me, look, I’ll fall for you, you know? Doing that, again… something like that… haha.”

To the short questions, the answering words from Subaru rang hollowly.

An emotion he himself understood to be empty words.

And then, Emilia gently brought her face close to that Subaru and,

“—It was… hard, wasn't it?”

“————!”

It was said as if to cherish him. It was said as if to comfort him. It was said as if to love him.

Just from that, just from that single phrase, the battered dam inside Subaru collapsed.

Breaking, tearing, what he had been holding back gushed out all at once.

It was the pent-up reservoir of intense emotion that he thought he had sealed away, but hadn’t been able to erase a single fragment of.

“It was… hard. It was so, painful. It was so scary. It was incredibly sad. It hurt so much I thought I would die…!”

“Yeah.”

“I, tried my best. I was trying my best. I was desperate. I was desperate to make everything better, I tried my best…! It’s true. Really, really, I’ve never tried this hard before in my life!”

“Yeah, I know.”

“Because I liked it, this place… because I thought it was important, this place…! So, I was desperate to get it back. I was scared. I was so scared. If they looked at me with those eyes again… I hated, hated myself for thinking that…!”

He couldn’t control his emotions.

Once it exploded, it overflowed as if a dam had broken, magnificently staining the face of the coward wearing the mask of a smile with tears.

The tears wouldn’t stop. Snot dripped down. Incomprehensible liquids overflowed in his mouth, turning Subaru’s sobbing voice into something even more agonizing to hear.

It was unseemly. It was pathetic. A grown man bawling on a girl’s lap while having his head stroked. It was so pathetic he wanted to die. His heart was so filled with warmth he thought he might die.

Emilia’s responses as she listened to Subaru’s complaints were gentle. Even if she said “I know,” it was an absolute given that not a single fragment of his experience had reached her.

And yet, Emilia’s voice carried a weight that he couldn’t just laugh off.

He didn’t know the reason. He might just want to think so.

But it was a fact that right now, Subaru felt as if he had been saved by that incomprehensible warmth.

Shedding buckets of tears, Subaru continued to cry on Emilia’s lap.

Crying, crying, wailing, until eventually the unseemly crying voice faded far away, and only quiet breathing fell in the guest room.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

—It was when Emilia was gently stroking the sleeping Subaru’s black hair that Rem visited that guest room.

Opening the door to the room without a sound, Rem found Emilia’s figure inside and was about to open her mouth when,

“Shh.”

She closed her mouth at Emilia’s gesture of pressing a finger to her lips.

Swaying her short-cut blue hair, Rem slowly looked around the room. Then, she walked over to the side of Emilia, who was sitting directly on the guest room floor with Subaru’s head on her lap, and,

“Is Subaru merely sleeping?”

“Yes. 

Fufu

, look, he’s like a child, isn’t he? When I stroke his head, he makes a face like he’s relieved.”

Stroking Subaru with amusement, Emilia sought Rem’s agreement. Rem responded to her request with a quiet shake of her head,

“It seems Subaru will not be able to do any more work today.”

“That’s right, he’s off today. Taking a day off after only working for two days, what a reaaally bad boy. Once he gets better, please kindly give him a punishment.”

Laughing softly, Emilia returned right back to her task of fiddling with Subaru’s face.

It seemed she had no intention of moving the sleeping Subaru to free her legs. Rem interpreted Emilia’s attitude as such and quietly looked down at him.

Innocently sleeping, the tension and frivolity had vanished from his expression.

For some reason, when he interacted with her sister and Rem, he would first overflow with a slight tension before floating a smile.

Sensing something profound in that attitude, Rem and her sister had been thinking of strengthening their surveillance posture, but.

“Seeing him sleeping like this makes one lose the motivation.”

Following Emilia, Rem lightly parted his bangs with her finger and muttered.

Defenseless like a baby. That figure, which seemed completely ignorant of the world, was rather pitiful, and Rem relaxed her lips just a tiny bit.

“Rem will go inform Sister that Subaru is useless today. We must redo the division of labor, kindly.”

Bowing, Rem politely left those words and turned her back.

Her destination was her sister’s location. If she closed her eyes, that location was immediately conveyed. She intended to head straight there and exchange words exactly as she had just said.

From behind her,

“Rem.”

Stopping her feet at the call, Rem slowly turned her whole body around.

The height of their gazes was vastly different from Emilia sitting on the floor. But even so, Rem felt a strange pressure, as if she were being looked down upon by Emilia.

Unaware of Rem’s slight surprise, Emilia quietly,

“—Subaru is a good boy, you know?”

At the words told to her, Rem responded with a deep bow.

Then, without leaving even a single glance, she headed for the door, leaving the two behind and exiting the guest room.

Walking down the hallway, she chewed over Emilia’s words from just now.

A slight tremor ran across the profile of the expressionless Rem, unnoticed even by herself.

—However, only the faintly wafting stench of evil left a slight lump in Rem’s heart.
